coreRule.es: No existe un único reloj: prescripción penal, prescripción civil, caducidad, responsabilidad del administrador concursal y responsabilidad patrimonial de la Administración de Justicia requieren análisis separados por acción, sujeto y acto.
coreRule.en: There is no single clock: criminal prescription, civil limitation, caducity, insolvency-administrator liability and administration-of-justice damages require separate claim-, party- and act-specific analysis.

clockClasses.rule: Period depends on the statutory maximum penalty and ordinarily runs from commission; special start rules apply to legally established continuing/permanent/habitual offences.
clockClasses.interruption: Judicial direction against a sufficiently identified suspected person interrupts; a court-filed complaint/querella naming a person can suspend computation for up to six months under art. 132.2 pending a qualifying judicial resolution.
clockClasses.boundary: Ordinary Fiscalía, police or administrative reporting must not be described as automatically interrupting criminal prescription.

clockClasses.basis: Código Civil arts. 1964, 1968, 1969, 1973; LECrim arts. 111, 114; Supreme Court same-facts criminal/civil doctrine
clockClasses.rule: Accrual and interruption depend on the cause of action. Same-facts criminal proceedings can delay commencement or interrupt civil prescription where they legally prevent or encompass the civil claim.
clockClasses.interruption: Court exercise, extrajudicial creditor demand or debtor acknowledgment under art. 1973; criminal proceedings can have additional same-facts effects under Supreme Court doctrine.
clockClasses.boundary: Not a universal tolling rule for every civil claim.

clockClasses.basis: Examples: CC arts. 1535 and 1524; LPH art. 18.3
clockClasses.rule: Strict short periods require their own trigger analysis.
clockClasses.boundary: Criminal proceedings do not automatically suspend caducity. LO 1/2025/MASC can be relevant to a live right only under its statutory conditions and does not automatically revive an expired right.

clockClasses.rule: Estate-damage administrator liability has a special four-year prescription framework tied to knowledge of damage and, in any event, cessation in office; direct individual actions remain separately preserved.
clockClasses.boundary: No single global AC limitation date; act, claimant, harm and action type must be separated.

clockClasses.rule: Judicial error and abnormal functioning have special procedural predicates and short periods, including the three-month error-declaration route and one-year compensation prescription.
clockClasses.boundary: Do not merge State liability with personal criminal allegations or publish exact deadline calculations without counsel review.

remedies: subsidiary public-entity civil liability where statutory conditions are met
restitution/resarcimiento from a participant for profit up to the value of participation
criminalRecovery.boundary: A later increase in hotel value is not automatically criminal proceeds, unjust enrichment or recoverable loss.

criminal: LECrim art. 589 security and embargo for possible pecuniary liabilities
LECrim art. 764 precautionary measures in abbreviated proceedings
CP art. 127 octies seizure/embargo/deposit to secure confiscation
civil: LPH art. 18.4 interim suspension of challenged Community resolutions
interimRelief.controlQuestion: What asset, title, income stream, evidence, Registry position or economic value could become harder to restore if no proportionate measure is taken before final judgment?

publicProhibitions: A Fiscalía complaint stops criminal prescription.
A criminal case freezes every civil deadline.
Ongoing economic harm means the offence is legally continuing.
All retracto/tanteo rights remain alive because there are criminal proceedings.
All insolvency-administrator acts share one limitation date.
A criminal allegation automatically freezes CAM/HNT/MYND assets.
The full current hotel value is automatically recoverable damages.
publicationRule: Do not publish conservative internal action dates or claim a clock status without identifying the exact legal basis, trigger and supporting act.
